Anti S.M.C. article published by the National Herald and other
local Chinese newspapers

The article entitled "Trade Associations Issue
Manifesto in Opposition to S.M.C. Rate Increase", which is
grossly anti-Council and inflammatory in tone, was published
on April 5, 1937, in all the principal Chinese daily newspapers,
with the exception of the Shun Pao which printed an abridged version.
Enquiries at the editorial office of the National Herald, 130
Ningpo Road, reveal that the information was received from the
Sin Sun (新聲) News Agency, Lane 420, House 9, Foochow Road,
which distributed mimeographed copies of the article to the
various newspapers for publication. The copy received by
the National Herald was shown to a member of the Special Branch
whose request for a loan of it was, however, refused. It is
said that the Sin Sun News Agency obtained the information
from either the Chinese Chamber of Commerce or the Chinese
Ratepayers' Association because Mr. Yen Ngon Sung (嚴彥聲)
Manager of the agency, is General Secretary of both of these
organisations.

Enquiries at the office of the Chinese Censorship
Board indicate that the censors did try to suppress the article
in its entirety, but owing to the opposition of the Chinese
press generally, they allowed the article to be published in
revised form, certain parts containing violent expressions being
deleted. The most objectionable part advocated a general strike
as the most effective weapon to bring the British people into
terms, quoting as example the strike which occurred in Hongkong
in 1927.

《国民日报》及其他本地中文报纸刊登的反工部局文章

题为“各同业公会发表宣言反对工部局加捐”的文章，其语气严重反对工部局且具有煽动性，于1937年4月5日在所有主要中文日报上刊登，唯独《申报》刊登了删节版。经向宁波路130号《国民日报》编辑部查询，获悉该消息系从福州路420弄9号的“新声”（Sin Sun）通讯社获得，该社将文章的油印副本分发给各家报纸予以刊登。《国民日报》收到的副本曾出示给特别支部的一名成员，但该成员借阅的请求遭到拒绝。据称，“新声”通讯社是从上海总商会或华人纳税会获得该消息的，因为该社经理严彦声（Yen Ngon Sung）先生同时担任这两个组织的秘书长。

经向中文新闻检查所查询，检查员确实试图完全查禁该文，但由于一般中文报界的反对，他们允许以修订形式刊登该文，删除了包含激烈言辞的某些部分。最令人反感的部分主张以总罢工作为迫使英国人妥协的最有效武器，并引用1927年发生在香港的罢工为例。

TRADE ASSOCIATIONS ISSUE MANIFESTO IN OPPOSITION
TO S.M.C. RATE INCREASE

One hundred and fifty local trade associations
including the Sea Products Dealers' Association, the Medicine
Dealers' Association, the Cotton Dealers' Association, the
Transportation Companies' Association, the Silk Dealers'
Association, the Ricsha Owners' Association, the Leather
Box Dealers' Association, the Candle Dealers' Association,
the Shoe Dealers' Association, the Wool Dealers' Association,
the Fish Hong Owners' Association, the Chinese Medicine
Store Owners' Association, the Foreign Dress Shop Owners'
Association, the Furniture Dealers' Association, the
Restaurant Owners' Association, the Egg Dealers' Association,
the Fur Dealers' Association and the Building Contractors'
Association, have jointly issued the following manifesto
opposing the increase in the Municipal Rate :-

"At a time when the livelihood of the citizens is
in a very depressed condition, the foreign lords who
fatten on the blood and sweat of the Chinese people are
utilizing the special influence of the Shanghai Municipal
Council Meeting to further their exploitation of us by
forcible and arbitrary means. The 14% Municipal Rate
has now been increased to 16%. This is one of the cruel
acts which the Imperialists so often commit.

"We do not express any fear, but we must not submit
like lambs to dismembering by others any longer. We
must firmly oppose the increase. Based on experience
and lessons we received in the past, we must act in unison,
otherwise we may get the same result as in our opposition
to the increase in telephone charges. We request the
whole body of citizens to unite and oppose the increase,
and to take practical action instead of arguing on paper."

各同业公会发表宣言反对工部局加捐

包括海产品经销商协会、药材经销商协会、棉花经销商协会、运输公司协会、丝绸经销商协会、人力车车主协会、皮箱经销商协会、蜡烛经销商协会、鞋类经销商协会、羊毛经销商协会、鱼行业主协会、中药店业主协会、洋服店业主协会、家具经销商协会、餐馆业主协会、蛋类经销商协会、皮草经销商协会和建筑承包商协会在内的150个本地同业公会，联合发表了以下反对增加市政捐税的宣言：

“在市民生计极度萧条之际，那些靠中国人民血汗养肥的外国老爷们，正利用上海工部局会议的特殊影响力，通过强制和任意的手段进一步剥削我们。市政捐税已从14%增加到16%。这是帝国主义者经常犯下的残酷行径之一。

“我们并不表示恐惧，但我们不能再像羔羊一样任人宰割。我们必须坚决反对加捐。基于我们过去获得的经验和教训，我们必须采取一致行动，否则我们可能会得到与反对电话费增加时相同的结果。我们请求全体市民团结起来反对加捐，并采取实际行动，而不是停留在纸面上的争论。”

(2)

If the S.M.C. refuses to rescind its decision for an
increase in the Municipal Rate, we will not forget, in
fact we will never forget about the general strike in
1927 when Hongkong was converted into Chuen Kong
(translator's note: characters "Hongkong" may mean
"perfumed river" while the meaning of "Chuen Kong" is
"stinking river"); we will never believe that the
authorities of the Shanghai Municipal Council are more
autocratic than those of Hongkong or that the strength
of the Shanghai inhabitants is inferior than that of
our brethren in Hongkong. We should use our full
energy in protesting against the increase in the Municipal
Rate.

"1927 was the year in which the Chinese people
roared. 1937 shall be the year of their emancipation.
Let us seize our opportunity, consider the situation and
fight all those enemies who exploit us. Let all who do
not wish to be slaves come swiftly under the flag of war".

-----

如果工部局拒绝撤销其增加市政捐税的决定，我们将不会忘记，事实上我们永远不会忘记1927年的总罢工，当时香港变成了‘臭港’（译者注：‘香港’二字可能意为‘香江’，而‘臭港’意为‘臭江’）；我们绝不相信上海工部局当局比香港当局更专制，也不相信上海居民的力量 inferior to（次于）我们在香港的同胞。我们应该全力以赴抗议市政捐税的增加。

“1927年是中国人民怒吼的一年。1937年将是他们获得解放的一年。让我们抓住机会，审时度势，打击所有剥削我们的敌人。让所有不愿做奴隶的人迅速集结在战旗之下”。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, TUESDAY, APRIL 27, 1937 2/40

COUNCIL TAXATION
A Critical Survey

To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"

SIR,—Late as this contribution of mine is towards the controversy over the proposed rate increase of the S.M.C. and its subsequent postponement, I hope, you will be kind enough to accord it the privileges of your valuable space. That I have given careful thought to all sides of the question will be, I trust too, apparent.

Some of the utterances of the representatives of the Chinese community here, like those of other nationalities, may be open to criticism. The letter of the Chinese Ratepayers Association, as appeared in your correspondence columns of the 14th instant, is, however, worthy of the same notice as the official statements in favour and in defence of the rate increase. It represents the attitude of the actual majority of the ratepaying population here; is a display of the anxiety for a close and amicable co-operation with the non-Chinese communities here; and contains nothing but constructive, though unavoidably recriminative, criticisms and suggestions. In particular, the following extract gives the logic of that attitude:

We believe that the present financial stringency of the Council is the accumulative result of over-spending in the past several years. It is only by holding tight our purse-string that the Council will be induced to exercise restraint and use discretion in the handling of public finance.

This need not be taken as a special slight on the integrity and competence of the Council; the tendency to extravagance on the part of the governing body, when additions to the revenue are readily available, is in no way peculiar to our, if not model then at least unique, Settlement; and an opposition to an increase in taxation, whether justified or not, should rather be welcomed as a salutary check on that tendency.

It feels like crying over spilled milk to dwell too much on the past of the Council's finance, but the figures brought up in the letter mentioned about the rapid increase of expenditures and items such as resignation payments, exchange compensations, etc., are not easily overlooked. Credit is, however, due to the old Council for having lately, in response to public agitation, effected quite noteworthy economy. And, under the pressure of that agitation, we may look forward with confidence to the new Council's efforts in further judicious retrenchments and avoidance of new commitments of unwarranted generosity.

The recommendation from Chinese and Japanese quarters for a more liberal employ of their nationals in the senior positions in the Council, to some extent already heeded, though savouring of partisanship, is, nevertheless, sound economically. Many Chinese, graduated in the best of universities, at home or abroad, are willing to work at what a mere clerk receives from S.M.C. I may cite a typical instance in Nanking, when 600 sat for the examination for four clerks at $80 monthly, among whom were several college graduates, including two returned students, one from Japan and one from the U.S.A.

In conclusion to those who are unacquainted with the distinction between Chinese and foreigners, we may remark that the former, unlike the latter, do not know to what extent, by those who cannot afford that dollar.

Your readers need not be alarmed at the prospect of my advocating Communistic or Bolshevik ideology; but, certainly, a more equitable way of collecting and spending may be asked. Indeed, it is useless to argue that Shanghai is the lowest taxed city of the world, for it is the return received in proportion to the tax paid that counts.

This inequity of indiscriminate taxation is really not so very insurmountable. It would indeed be most desirable, if something akin to the Income Tax were introduced here too. Failing this, an accumulative scale of the rates could be considered. As to the spending, the interest that the Council has taken in problems such as Rickshaw, Housing, Food, etc., does promise a brighter future for the bulk, the poorer strata, of the population here. It is hoped that foreigners will join forces in pressing the new Council for more energetic progress and more concrete results in that direction.

U. K.
Shanghai, Apr. 25.

During the times of critical finance of 1932/3, Chinese governmental offices have introduced salary cuts sliding upwards to 50 per cent. That, of course, may be overdoing a good thing; but the S.M.C. surely would be able to find a more equitable gold mean. At the present, when prosperity is as yet around the corner, few would be optimistic enough to expect to escape the pinch of depression. We have seen times when no self-respecting foreign girl typist would work for less than $150, but now we have applications from foreign males pouring in asking for $40 upwards, with nary a one audacious enough to aspire to over $100. What is sauce for the goose without the Council is certainly sauce for the gander within. As to the senior officer of the S.M.C., it is only to remember that, not so many weeks ago, some British members of the Cabinet received as little as £2,000 annually.

工部局捐税
一项批判性审视

致《字林西报》编辑：

先生，——尽管本人就工部局拟议增加捐税及其随后延期一事所引发的争议投稿较晚，仍望阁下惠予刊登于贵报宝贵版面。相信本人已对问题的各个方面进行了深思熟虑，这一点想必也是显而易见的。

此地华人社区代表的一些言论，如同其他国籍人士一样，或许值得商榷。然而，本月14日刊于贵报读者来信栏的华人纳税会信函，却值得与那些支持和辩护加税的官方声明受到同等关注。它代表了此地实际大多数纳税居民的态度；展现了与本地非华人社群紧密友好合作的愿望；并且除了建设性的、尽管不可避免地带有指责性质的批评和建议外，别无他物。特别是以下摘录阐明了该态度的逻辑：

我们认为，工部局目前的财政拮据是过去几年超支累积的结果。只有紧紧捂住钱袋子，才能促使工部局在公共财政管理上行使克制并运用裁量权。

这不必被视为对工部局廉洁和能力的特别轻视；当收入来源容易增加时，管理机构倾向于铺张浪费，这种现象绝非我们这一虽非模范但至少独特的租界所独有；而对增税的反对，无论是否正当，都应被视为对这种倾向的一种有益制约而受到欢迎。

过多沉湎于工部局过去的财务状况犹如为打翻的牛奶哭泣，但前述信函中提到的支出迅速增长以及离职金、汇兑补偿等项目的数据，却不容忽视。不过，老工部局近期响应公众舆论，实施了相当显著的节约措施，这点值得肯定。而且，在这种舆论压力下，我们可以有信心期待新工部局进一步审慎削减开支，并避免做出不必要的慷慨承诺。

来自中方和日方建议在工部局高级职位中更广泛地任用其本国国民，这一建议在一定程度上已得到采纳，虽然带有党派色彩，但在经济上是合理的。许多毕业于国内外顶尖大学的中国人，愿意从事仅相当于工部局普通职员薪水的工作。我可以举一个南京的典型例子：当时有600人参加每月薪金80元的四个职员职位的考试，其中包括几名大学毕业生，包括两名归国留学生，一名来自日本，一名来自美国。

最后，对于那些不了解华人与外国人区别的人，我们可以指出，前者不像后者那样，不知道那一美元对那些负担不起的人来说意味着什么程度。

读者不必因我似乎倡导共产主义或布尔什维克意识形态而感到惊慌；但是，确实可以要求一种更公平的征收和使用方式。的确，争论上海是世界上税率最低的城市是没有用的，因为重要的是相对于所缴税款而言获得的回报。

这种不加区分的征税所造成的不公并非真的那么难以克服。如果这里也能引入类似所得税的制度，那将是最理想的。若做不到这一点，可以考虑采用累进税率。至于支出方面，工部局对人力车、住房、食品等问题的关注，确实为此地占人口大多数的较贫困阶层带来了更光明的未来。希望外国人也联合起来，向新工部局施压，要求在这一方向上取得更有力的进展和更具体的成果。

U. K.
上海，4月25日。

在1932/33年财政危机时期，中国政府机构曾实行高达50%的减薪。当然，这可能有些矫枉过正；但工部局肯定能够找到一个更公平的金科玉律（中庸之道）。目前，繁荣尚指日可待，很少有人乐观到足以期望摆脱萧条的压力。我们曾见过自尊的外国女打字员薪水低于150元就不愿工作的时期，但现在外国男性的申请纷至沓来，索要40元以上的薪水，竟无一人胆敢奢望超过100元。既然对工部局外部人员适用的规则，对内部人员也应当适用。至于工部局的高级官员，只需记住，就在几周前，英国内阁的一些成员年薪仅为2,000英镑。

工部局以及外国纳税人会议，不应受到责难，反而应因其以延期和可能重新审议的形式达成妥协而受到赞扬。确实令人欣慰地注意到，随着大多数华人表现出合作与妥协的意愿，许多外国人也意识到，如果要使这个国际都市顺利运转并造福所有人，就必须有更多的国际和谐与团结，减少外国人对抗华人的情结。

工部局卸任主席阿诺德（Arnhold）先生曾多次指出，拟议的增加额仅相当于每10元房租估值的30分。对此，请允许我说，这些金额“虽然本身很小，但与支付这些金额的收入的相比，代表了一笔沉重的开支”，引用贵报近期关于中国所得税的评论。

可以断言，华人纳税会所代表的，更多的是那些无声的、无投票权的、缴纳零碎税款的纳税人，而非其会员。至于有投票权的会员，我相信，其中不少人向慈善和其他公共基金捐赠的金额，已是拟议增加额的许多倍。就个人而言，我认为即使增加20%也无害处，只要它不对那些缴纳零碎税款的人产生不利影响，并且新增收入得到妥善使用。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, WEDNESDAY, APRIL 14, 1937.
COUNCIL FINANCE
Chinese Ratepayers' Views
To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
SIR,—Constitutional anomaly of the Settlement, legacy of the antiquated past, has kept Chinese and Foreign Ratepayers apart. We are yet de-barred from meeting each other in one assembly and discussing ques-tions of common interest on the floor of the same house. This open letter is the medium through which we hope to acquaint you with our views as regards the proposed increase in the General and Special Municipal Rates and correlative Land Tax there-on originally fixed to take effect on July 1, in the current year, but now postponed for a period of six months.
The Chinese Ratepayers are rea-sonably sure that the Council could, if it only would, balance its Budget without having to have recourse to increased taxation. After a close scrutiny of the Municipal Budget, the Chinese Ratepayers believe that the Council's assessment of its income especially in respect to the rates is made on too pessimistic a basis while the measures of economy aiming at curtailment of expenditure are half-hearted and taken with incorrect em-phasis.
It must be pointed out that the revenue derivable from the rates constitutes a highly stable and re-liable source of income to the Coun-cil which for the past one decade, no further, had shown steady and regulated increase year by year. The only drop occurred in 1935 when a decrease of $700,000 was recorded. This, however, happened solely in the first half year. In the second half, the tendency to recover soon showed itself, and the collection was 101 per cent. as compared with that for the corresponding half year of 1935 on cash basis and 98 per cent. on ac-crued basis. It is therefore within reason to predict for 1937 a receipt from this source, of an amount at least approximating the 1935 figure and with the record of the past de-cade as our indication reinforced by growing sign of economic recovery the expectation that the collection may even rise and begin to resume its normal rate of increase is cer-tainly not inspired by undue opti-mism.
This steady increase of the Council's income was counteracted by a similar and at times greater increase in its expenditure. The present pre-carious financial position is due principally to the fact that during the years 1930 and 1931 while there was only normal increase in income there occurred an abnormal and dis-proportionate large increase in ex-penditure. And in 1936, while the total income showed a decrease of $320,000 as compared with that for 1935, the total expenditure had shown an increase of approximately $1,200,000 over the 1935 figure. If it is remembered that the Coun-cil is being owed from arrears in rates a startling sum of $2,000,000 similar in amount to that which it hopes to raise through increased taxation, the basic reason for the present financial stringency is not far to seek.
Of course, there have been instances of economy. While we note that a saving of $200,000 has been effected from reductions in the cost of the Fire Brigade and of $50,000 from abolition of the post of Deputy Commissioner of Police, we feel that these economies are insufficient to offset the heavy increases in other directions.
It must be emphasized that the Council's undue generosity to its senior staff has evoked comment in the foreign no less than in the Chinese communities. Similar views on the subject have found ventilation in Chinese and foreign press alike. As regards the proposed aboli-tion of the Municipal Band and Orchestra, a cultural amenity in time of prosperity but a luxury in times of stress, this has been sponsored by the Chinese as well as by a large body of the foreign community; and so is the mooted disbandment of the Russian Detachment which is aptly described by our foreign critic as a "Toy Army" too imposing in time of peace but too inadequate for pur-pose of war. The rapid increase in the expenditures of the principal Departments, especially the Police, the cost of which in 1929 was $5,500,000 but rose to $9,620,000 in 1931, an increase of $4,000,00 in two years, has, we are sure, shocked the Chinese and foreign Ratepayers alike who concur in the question "Is there any limit to the expansion?"
It will be seen therefore that in vetoing the proposed increase and bringing to light the foregoing, the Chinese Ratepayers are in no way motivated by egoistic considerations, but are simply responding to the candid and judicious opinion of the foreign community. The Chairman of the Council in seeking to justify the increase has emphasized its meagreness and pointed out that to the resident paying a rental of $10 per month the increase means only twenty cents. We wish our foreign friends to understand that the dis-approval of the Chinese Ratepayers is not based on any pecuniary con-sideration such as the Chairman appears to insinuate. We believe that the present financial stringency of the Council is the accumulated result of over-spending in the past several years. It is only by holding tight our purse string that the Coun-cil will be induced to exercise re-straint and use discretion in the handling of public finance. There is a principle involved, and the fact that Shanghai is the lowest taxed city in the world is no reason why Shanghai should be taxed higher.
It is gratifying that the Council has finally deemed necessary to accept an amendment to the Budget whereby the increase will be postponed for a period of six months. At our Annual Meeting, we adopted an amended re-solution:
"Resolved that consideration of in-creases in the General and Special Municipal Rates and correlative Land Tax thereof be held in abeyance until next year, and that the Council be urged to take adequate steps to curtail un-necessary expenses and recover rates, taxes and dues, which are in arrears in the course of the current year."
The import of the resolution is clear. The Chinese Ratepayers will welcome a similar resolution from the Foreign Ratepayers in spirit and in effect if not necessarily in letter.
SHAI CHINESE RATEPAYERS ASSOC.
Shanghai April 14.

工部局财政
华人纳税人的观点
致《字林西报》编辑先生：

先生，——租界宪制上的反常现象，乃是陈旧过去的遗留物，致使华人与外籍纳税人彼此隔绝。我们仍被禁止在同一集会中会面，并在同一议事厅内讨论共同关心的问题。这封公开信是我们希望向阁下告知我们对拟议增加一般市政捐、特别市政捐及相应土地税（原定于本年7月1日生效，现推迟六个月）之看法的媒介。

华人纳税人有理由确信，工部局若有意为之，本可在不诉诸增税的情况下平衡其预算。在仔细审查市政预算后，华人纳税人认为，工部局对其收入（尤其是捐税方面）的评估基于过于悲观的基础，而旨在削减支出的节约措施则半心半意，且重点把握不当。

必须指出，捐税所得收入构成了工部局高度稳定且可靠的收入来源，在过去十年间，该收入显示出逐年稳步且有规律的增长。唯一的下降发生在1935年，当时记录了70万美元的减少。然而，这仅发生在上半年。下半年，复苏趋势很快显现，按现金基础计算，征收额达到1935年相应半年的101%，按应计基础计算则为98%。因此，预测1937年从此来源获得的收入至少接近1935年的数额是合乎情理的；并且，以过去十年的记录为指引，加之经济复苏迹象日益明显，预期征收额甚至可能上升并开始恢复其正常增长率，这肯定并非出于过度的乐观。

工部局收入的这种稳步增长被其支出类似、有时甚至更大的增长所抵消。目前岌岌可危的财务状况主要归因于以下事实：在1930年和1931年期间，收入仅有正常增长，而支出却出现了异常且不成比例的大幅增加。而在1936年，虽然总收入较1935年减少了32万美元，但总支出较1935年的数字增加了约120万美元。如果记得工部局因拖欠捐税而被欠付一笔惊人的200万美元款项，其金额与它希望通过增税筹集的金额相当，那么造成目前财政紧张的基本原因就不难找到了。

当然，也有节约的例子。虽然我们注意到，通过降低消防队费用节省了20万美元，并通过废除警务处副总监一职节省了5万美元，但我们认为这些节约不足以抵消其他方面的大幅增加。

必须强调，工部局对其高级职员的过度慷慨已在华人和外籍社群中均引发议论。中外报刊对此均有类似观点的表达。关于拟议取消工部局乐队和管弦乐团一事——这在繁荣时期是一种文化便利，但在困难时期则是一种奢侈——这得到了华人以及大部分外籍社群的支持；同样受到支持的还有拟议解散俄国分队之举，我们的外籍评论员恰当地将其描述为一支“玩具军队”，在和平时期显得过于铺张，但在战争目的上又过于不足。主要部门支出的迅速增加，特别是警务处，其费用在1929年为550万美元，但在1931年升至962万美元，两年内增加了400多万美元，我们相信这震惊了华人和外籍纳税人，他们一致质疑：“扩张是否有止境？”

因此可以看出，华人纳税人在否决拟议的增税并揭示上述情况时，绝非受自私考虑驱动，而只是回应外籍社群坦诚且明智的意见。工部局主席在试图为增税辩护时，强调了其幅度之微小，并指出对于每月支付租金10元的住户来说，增税意味着仅增加2角钱。我们希望我们的外籍朋友理解，华人纳税人的反对并非基于主席似乎暗示的任何金钱考量。我们认为，工部局目前的财政紧张是过去几年过度支出的累积结果。只有紧紧捂住钱袋，才能促使工部局在处理公共财政时行使克制并运用审慎判断。这里涉及一个原则，上海作为世界上税负最低的城市这一事实，并不是上海应该被征收更高税额的理由。

令人欣慰的是，工部局最终认为有必要接受一项对预算的修正案，据此增税将推迟六个月。在我们的年度会议上，我们通过了一项经修正的决议：
“决议：暂缓考虑增加一般市政捐、特别市政捐及相应土地税，直至明年；并敦促工部局采取适当步骤，在本年度内削减不必要的开支，并追收拖欠的捐税及费用。”
该决议的含义是明确的。如果外籍纳税人能在精神上和实质效果上（而不必在字面上）通过类似的决议，华人纳税人将表示欢迎。

上海华人纳税人协会
上海，4月14日。

THE CHINA PRESS. WEDNESDAY APRIL 14,
EQUAL REPRESENTATION
（批：2/2h）
（批：7803）
A T the annual meeting on Monday, the Chinese Ratepayers Association touched upon various municipal problems. Mr. Wang Hsiao-lai, Chairman of the Association, made a most explicit analysis of municipal finance and observed that "If the Council could be led to dispense with the non-essential services and economise further in personnel expenses the deficit could have been easily met."
The discussion of the municipal budget, however illuminating, may be omitted for fear of repetition. The subject which should engage the serious attention of all residents, Chinese and foreign alike, is the Chinese demand for equal representation in municipal affairs. This demand is by no means new, but with the change of local conditions it is bound to gather more momentum with the passage of time.
Time was when the Chinese had no councillors of their own on the Council. Though official representation has now been realised to a limited extent, the foreign councillors are still in the majority and enjoy a commanding vote as against that of the Chinese. This inequity is hardly tenable in view of the preponderantly higher percentage of tax which the Chinese community pays annually into the municipal coffer.
A greater inequity, however, is to be witnessed in the absolute lack of voice in municipal problems on the part of the Chinese Ratepayers' Association. Each year the municipal budget, only to cite a notable instance, is submitted for approval to the Foreign Ratepayers' Meeting, but it is not so submitted to that of the Chinese. For all practical purposes the Chinese Ratepayers' Association is but an electorate for Chinese councillors each year besides exercising a few functions of minor importance among the Chinese themselves.
It is only logical, therefore, that the Chinese ratepayers should desire to make their Association an effective organ through which the administration of the International Settlement may be controlled in partnership with its sister association representing the foreign community. This desire, needless to point out, is well founded on more than one ground.
The amount of the municipal rate paid by the Chinese, as has often been suggested, should entitle the Chinese to as much effective voice in municipal matters as the foreign nationals regardless of its actual percentage. The principle of taxation without representation is not a sound principle which may be adopted in an international community like Shanghai; it is a principle which has already given rise to much misunderstanding and is capable of working greater mischief in the future.
From the population standpoint, the number of Chinese residents in the Settlement is much larger than that of all foreigners combined. If any national group is entitled to exercise control over municipal administration, it is clearly the Chinese. The monopoly enjoyed by the Foreign Ratepayers' Meeting in the exercise of legislative power over the Council cannot be defended on the basis of equity or of elementary democratic principles.
From the standpoint of Chinese investment in the Settlement, we are sure that the Chinese are entitled to an effective representation in municipal affairs as much as, if not more than, all the foreign national groups put together. It may be added in passing that a major portion of the land in the Settlement, while registered under foreign names, is actually owned by the Chinese, and the question of taxation which so vitally affects them should certainly not be left entirely to the discretion of foreigners whose interest in Shanghai's future is at best of a transient nature.

平等代表权
（批注：2/2h）
（批注：7803）

在周一的年度会议上，华人纳税人协会触及了各种市政问题。协会主席王晓籁先生对市政财政作了极为明确的分析，并指出：“如果能促使工部局裁撤非必要的服务，并在人员经费上进一步节约，赤字本可轻易弥补。”

对市政预算的讨论虽具启发性，但为避免重复，此处从略。所有居民，无论华人还是外籍人士，都应认真关注的议题，是华人要求在市政事务中享有平等代表权。这一要求绝非新事，但随着本地形势的变化，随着时间的推移，它必将积聚更多的动力。

曾几何时，华人在工部局中没有自己的董事。虽然目前在有限程度上实现了官方代表权，但外籍董事仍占多数，并与华人董事相比拥有压倒性的投票权。鉴于华人社群每年向市政金库缴纳的税款比例占绝对优势，这种不公正是难以站得住脚的。

然而，更大的不公正体现在华人纳税人协会在市政问题上完全缺乏发言权。仅举一个显著例子，每年的市政预算都提交给外籍纳税人会议批准，但却未提交给华人纳税人会议。就实际目的而言，华人纳税人协会不过是每年选举华人董事的一个选民团体，此外仅在华人内部行使一些次要职能。

因此，华人纳税人希望使其协会成为一个有效机构，通过与代表外籍社群的姊妹协会合作，共同控制国际租界的行政管理，这是合乎逻辑的。毋庸赘言，这一愿望有着多方面的充分依据。

正如经常有人指出的那样，华人缴纳的市政捐数额，应使华人在市政事务中享有与外籍人士同等的有效发言权，无论其实际百分比如何。“无代表不纳税”的原则不是一个可以在像上海这样的国际社群中采用的健全原则；这是一个已经引起诸多误解的原则，并且有可能在未来造成更大的危害。

从人口角度来看，租界内的华人居民数量远远超过所有外籍人士的总和。如果有任何民族群体有权对市政行政管理行使控制权，那显然是华人。外籍纳税人会议在对工部局行使立法权方面的垄断，无法基于公平或基本民主原则进行辩护。

从华人在租界投资的角度来看，我们确信，华人在市政事务中享有的有效代表权至少应与所有外籍民族群体的总和相当，甚至更多。顺便提一下，租界内的大部分土地虽然登记在外籍人名下，但实际上由华人拥有，如此切身影响他们的税务问题，当然不应完全留给那些对上海未来的利益至多具有短暂性质的外籍人士去酌情决定。

For these and other reasons the demand of the Chinese to exercise a control over municipal administration on an equal basis with the foreign ratepayers cannot be rejected without outraging the sense of fair play. What is more, the development of the Civic Center cannot but produce far-reaching effect on the Settlement itself. It would be highly advisable to enlist the support of the local Chinese residents for the purpose of co-ordinating official Chinese endeavor with that of the Council in the future growth of Shanghai as a whole. Chinese voice in municipal matters, in other words, will help to eliminate all possible conflict of interests between the Settlement and the Chinese Municipality of Greater Shanghai, while its absence is sure to dampen Chinese enthusiasm for the continued existence of the Settlement itself.
For the sake of closer Sino-foreign co-operation the legitimate aspirations of the Chinese should be heeded without further ado. The Chinese bear the lion's share in municipal progress; they should enjoy a fair share in the control over municipal administration. The demand is not exorbitant; it is the minimum condition in any self-respecting municipal government or quasi-municipal government.

出于这些及其他原因，华人要求在与外籍纳税人平等的基础上对市政行政管理行使控制权的要求，若被拒绝，将严重违背公平竞争的精神。此外，大上海市中心区的发展必然会对租界本身产生深远影响。为了协调中国官方的努力与工部局在上海整体未来发展中的工作，争取当地华人居民的支持将是极为明智的。换言之，华人在市政事务中的声音将有助于消除租界与大上海华界之间所有可能的利益冲突，而其缺失肯定会打击华人对租界继续存在的热情。

为了更紧密的中外合作，应当立即重视华人的合理诉求。华人在市政进步中承担了最大份额的责任；他们应在市政行政管理的控制中享有公平的份额。这一要求并不过分；它是任何自尊的市政府或准市政府的最低条件。

OPEN LETTER TO FOREIGN RATEPAYERS
The following Open Letter to Foreign Ratepayers has been addressed to this journal by the Shanghai Chinese Ratepayers Association:
Fellow Ratepayers.—The constitutional anomaly of the Settlement, legacy of the antiquated past, has kept Chinese and Foreign Ratepayers apart. We are yet debarred from meeting each other in one assembly and discussing questions of common interest on the floor of the same house. This Open Letter is the medium through which we hope to acquaint you with our views as regards the proposed increase in the General and Special Municipal Rates and correlative Land Tax thereon, originally fixed to take effect on July 1, in the current year, but now postponed for a period of six months.
The Chinese Ratepayers are reasonably sure that the Council could, if it only would, balance its Budget without having recourse to increased taxation. After a close scrutiny of the Municipal Budget, the Chinese Ratepayers believe that the Council's assessment of its income, especially in respect to the rates, is made on too pessimistic a basis, while the measures of economy aiming at curtailment of expenditure are half-hearted and taken with incorrect emphasis.
It must be pointed out that the revenue derivable from the rates constitutes a highly stable and reliable source of income to the Council which for the past decade, if no farther, had shown steady and regulated increase year by year. The only drop occurred in 1936, when a decrease of $700,000 was recorded. This, however, happened solely in the first half year. In the second half, the tendency to recover soon showed itself, and the collection was 101 per cent. as compared with that for the corresponding half year of 1935 on cash basis and 98 per cent. on accrued basis. It is therefore within reason to predict for 1937 a receipt, from this source, of an amount at least approximating the 1935 figure, and, with the record of the past decade as our indication, reinforced by growing signs of economic recovery, the expectation, that the collection may even rise and begin to resume its normal rate of increase is certainly not inspired by undue optimism.
Raising Expenditure
This steady increase of the Council's income was counteracted by a similar and at times greater increase in its expenditure. The present precarious financial position is due principally to the fact that during the years 1930 and 1931, while there was only normal increase, in income, there occurred an abnormal and disproportionately large increase in expenditure. And in 1936, while the total income showed a decrease of $300,000 as compared with that for 1935; the total expenditure had shown an increase of approximately $1,300,000 over the 1935 figure. If it is remembered that the Council is being owed from arrears in rates a startling sum of $3,800,000, similar in amount to that which it hopes to raise through increased taxation, the basic reason for the present financial stringency is not far to seek.
Of course, there have been measures of economy. While we note that a saving of $200,000 has been effected from reduction in the cost of the Fire Brigade and of $100,000 from abolition of superfluous offices, we also note that a lump sum of the former amount was paid to its Commissioner of Works on retirement; and, of the latter amount, to its Secretary on resignation. while it is true that the Council will save $1,060,000 from staff economy, it is equally true that it will perpetuate a temporary benefit of exchange compensation amounting, in 1936, to $1,880,000 and grant new exchange compensation to more than 90 Class "A" employees.
Band And Orchestra
It must be emphasized that the Council's undue generosity to its senior staff has evoked comment in the foreign no less than in the Chinese communities. Similar views on the subject have found ventilation in Chinese and foreign press alike. As regards the proposed abolition of the Municipal Band and Orchestra, a cultural amenity in time of prosperity but a luxury in time of stress, this abolition has been sponsored by the Chinese as well as by a large body of the foreign community and so is the mooted disbandment of the Russian Detachment which is aptly described by one foreign critic as a "Toy Army" too imposing in time of peace but too inadequate for purposes of war. The rapid increase in the expenditures of the principal Departments, especially the Police, the cost of which in 1929 was $5,-500,000 but rose to $9,620,000 in 1931, an increase of $4,000,000 in two years, has, we are sure, shocked the Chinese and foreign Ratepayers alike who concur in the question "Is there any limit to the expansion?"
It will be seen therefore that in vetoing the proposed increase and bringing to light the foregoing, the Chinese Ratepayers are in no way motivated by egoistic considerations, but are simply responding to the candid and judicious opinion of the foreign community. The Chairman of the Council, in seeking to justify the increase has emphasized its meagreness and pointed out that to the resident paying a rental of $10 per month the increase means only 20 cents. We wish our foreign friends to understand that the disapproval of the Chinese Ratepayers is not based on any pecuniary consideration such as the Chairman appears to insinuate. We believe that the present financial stringency of the Council is the accumulated result of over-spending in the past several years. It is only by holding tight our purse string that Council will be induced to exercise restraint and use discretion in the handling of public finance. There is a principle involved, and the fact that Shanghai is the lowest taxed city in the world is no reason why Shanghai should be taxed higher.
It is gratifying that the Council has finally deemed it necessary to accept an amendment to the Budget whereby the increase will be postponed for a period of six months. At our Annual Meeting, we adopted an amended resolution:
"Resolved that consideration of increase in the General and Special Municipal Rate, and correlative Land Tax thereon such as proposed by the Council be held in abeyance until next year, and that the Council be ordered to take adequate steps to curtail unnecessary expenses and recover rates, taxes and dues which are in arrears in the course of the current year."
The purport of the resolution is clear. The Chinese Ratepayers will welcome a similar resolution from you in spirit and in effect if not necessarily in letter.
SHANGHAI CHINESE RATEPAYERS ASSOCIATION.
Shanghai, April 13, 1937.

致外国纳税人的公开信
上海华人纳税人协会向本报致函，刊登如下致外国纳税人的公开信：

各位纳税人同仁——租界宪制上的反常现象，乃是陈旧过往的遗留物，致使华洋纳税人彼此隔绝。我们仍被禁止在同一集会中相聚，并在同一议事厅内讨论共同关心的议题。本公开信旨在作为媒介，希望使诸位了解我们就拟议增加一般市政捐、特别市政捐及相应土地税所持的观点；上述增税原定于本年7月1日生效，现已推迟六个月。

华人纳税人有充分理由确信，工部局若有意为之，完全可以在不增加税收的情况下平衡预算。在仔细审查市政预算后，华人纳税人认为，工部局对其收入的评估，尤其是关于捐税收入的评估，基于过于悲观的基础；而其旨在削减支出的节约措施则缺乏诚意，且重点失当。

必须指出，捐税收入构成工部局一项高度稳定且可靠的收入来源。至少在过去十年间，该收入显示出逐年稳步且规律的增长。唯一的下降出现在1936年，录得减少70万美元。然而，这仅发生在上半年。下半年很快显现出复苏趋势，按现金收付制计算，征收额达到1935年同期的101%，按权责发生制计算则为98%。因此，预测1937年从此来源获得的收入至少接近1935年的水平是合乎情理的；而且，以过去十年的记录为指引，加之经济复苏迹象日益明显，预期征收额甚至可能上升并开始恢复其正常增长率，这绝非出于过度的乐观。

支出增加

工部局收入的稳步增长被其支出的类似、有时甚至更大的增长所抵消。目前岌岌可危的财政状况，主要归因于1930年和1931年间，收入仅正常增长，而支出却出现异常且不成比例的大幅增加。而在1936年，虽然总收入较1935年减少了30万美元，但总支出较1935年的数字增加了约130万美元。如果记得工部局因拖欠捐税而被欠付一笔惊人的380万美元，其数额与它希望通过增税筹集的金额相当，那么造成当前财政紧张的基本原因便不难寻找。

当然，也曾采取过节约措施。虽然我们注意到，通过降低消防队成本节省了20万美元，通过裁撤冗余职位节省了10万美元，但我们也注意到，前一笔金额中的一笔整款支付给了退休的工务局局长；后一笔金额中的一笔整款支付给了辞职的秘书。诚然，工部局将通过人员精简节省106万美元，但同样属实的是，它将延续一项临时性的汇兑补偿福利，该福利在1936年达188万美元，并将向90多名“A”类雇员发放新的汇兑补偿。

乐队与管弦乐团

必须强调，工部局对高级职员过度的慷慨已在华洋社群中均引发议论。中外报刊对此均发表了类似观点。关于拟议撤销市政乐队和管弦乐团一事——这在繁荣时期是一种文化便利，而在困难时期则是一种奢侈——华人以及大量外国社群成员均支持此项撤销；同样，人们也主张解散俄国分队，一位外国评论家恰当地将其描述为一支“玩具军队”，在和平时期显得过于铺张，而在战争目的上则过于不足。主要部门支出的迅速增加，尤其是警务处，其费用在1929年为550万美元，但在1931年升至962万美元，两年内增加了400万美元，我们相信，这令华洋纳税人均感到震惊，大家一致质疑：“扩张是否有止境？”

由此可见，华人纳税人在否决拟议的增税并揭示上述事实时，绝非受自私动机驱使，而只是回应外国社群坦诚且明智的意见。工部局主席在试图为增税辩护时，强调其增幅微薄，并指出对于每月支付租金10美元的住户而言，增税仅意味着20美分。我们希望外国朋友理解，华人纳税人的反对并非基于主席似乎暗示的任何金钱考量。我们认为，工部局目前的财政紧张是过去几年过度支出的累积结果。只有紧紧捂住钱袋，才能促使工部局在处理公共财政时行使克制并运用审慎判断。这其中涉及原则问题，而上海作为世界上税负最低的城市这一事实，并不能成为上海应当承受更高税负的理由。

令人欣慰的是，工部局最终认为有必要接受一项预算修正案，从而将增税推迟六个月。在我们的年度会议上，我们通过了一项修正决议：

“决议：暂缓审议工部局所提议的一般市政捐、特别市政捐及相应土地税的增加事宜，直至明年；并责令工部局在本年度内采取适当措施，削减不必要开支，并追缴拖欠的捐税及费用。”

该决议的主旨清晰明了。如果外国纳税人能在精神上和实质上（即便不一定在文字上）通过类似的决议，华人纳税人将表示欢迎。

上海华人纳税人协会
1937年4月13日，上海

REC STNY
Rate Raise Postponement
ALL THINGS CONSIDERED, the Shanghai Municipal Council's decision for a compromise postponement of the proposed rate increase from July 1 to January 1 is probably the best way out of a bad situation even though it stands as one more monument to expediency. The Settlement desperately needs the money from extra rates, but it does not need a strike of Chinese ratepayers and that appears to have been the unavoidable alternative to postponement.

On the face of it, the attitude of the Chinese ratepayers has been thoroughly selfish and wrong-headed. But on the other hand many of these same Chinese ratepayers have been undergoing economic punishment beside which any potential difficulties of the hitherto well-financed Council must seem to them as nothing.

The findings of the Council's own Housing Commission are well worth re-examination by anyone who doubts that many thousands of Chinese in Shanghai are in a desperate plight economically—a plight where the payment of an extra dollar or an extra twenty cents looms up mountain-high.

In Shanghai, says the Sub-Committee on Economic Aspects, "probably no industrial family is adequately housed." People do not submit to inadequate housing because they enjoy it but because they are on a sub-subsistence level of existence. If they had money enough to pay more rates they would spend that money instantly on better lodging, or food. The "typical monthly family income of wage-earners" is found to be about $25, of which only about $5 a month can be paid in rent, or around $1 per head. Even more significant is Appendix III in which it is declared: "It is found that neither the unskilled, nor semi-skilled, nor the skilled workers live within the wage earned" with the result that a whole population is sinking gradually into debt.

That is not a picture of people who can be expected to look with equanimity upon any slightest increase in living costs. Their reaction is to bare their teeth and fight; and can we blame them? If their education stretches to include some knowledge of municipal problems, even this is not likely to inspire them with desire to pay more rates with knowledge that their own thin time is not to be rather more closely matched than hitherto by those to share proceeds of those additional rates. Needless to say, such amenities as the municipal orchestra are so far above their comprehension that we may dismiss them from all calculation; yet we cannot dismiss from calculation their perhaps nebulous, yet tenaciously clung-to conviction that nobody else in the vicinity is quite as badly off as are they—the Chinese workers of Shanghai.

Yet on the other hand no one will urge that the level of the masses of Shanghai industrial workers should determine the level of administration in the Settlement. Any step even bordering upon such an admission would...

The one thing which can be done is already being done in degree: To make the administration of Settlement affairs as business-like and economical as possible, and in particular to lose no opportunity to serve the special interest of the Chinese who after all both outnumber the foreign residents but likewise pay a majority of the Settlement's rate income.

It seems to us that in such matters as supporting the project of a diet kitchen experiment during this coming summer, the Council has been thoroughly on the right track. That project is small, but significant; from it can come much of tremendous benefit to underprivileged Chinese who are now subject to malnutrition and diet deficiency diseases which we are told can be overcome without extra cost for food if only the right foods, and methods of preparation, can be propagandized after suitable experiment which has been provided for. Publicity for such projects as this, in the Chinese press, should go a long way toward showing Chinese ratepayers that the Council is awake to Chinese needs.

We have no hesitation in saying that the record of the settlement has been consistently one of growing awareness of the necessity for giving Chinese residents of this area their just due, and perhaps (in such things as education) rather more than their exact due on a proportion of rates paid. But this fact must be made known, and where compromise can be achieved without surrender here should be an avoidance of costly clashes.

It is on this last ground, if no other, that justification for the present rate postponement can be found. This is not a time to provoke a fight by even the appearance of arbitrary action. We credit the Chinese Council members with full good faith in their undertaking to support the rate increase if given additional time, and it must be quite largely their task to show their people that such increase is necessary. Such a task will not be easy, considering the economic position of many of the Chinese in the Settlement, and it must be handled with a firmness well diluted by tact and particularly by such methods of propaganda as may be at hand for educating the Chinese ratepayers concerning the full facts.

More than ever before, it will be necessary that these facts be open to the public and susceptible to the closest examination. Chinese are canny buyers and not given to purchase of "a pig in a poke". To them, a raise in rates is a matter where salesmanship is required—and the commodity is good government, trimmed with a new and welcome growing consciousness of social responsibility.

税率上调延期
通盘考虑之下，上海公共租界工部局决定妥协，将拟议的税率上调从7月1日推迟至1月1日，这或许是摆脱困境的最佳出路，尽管此举不过是权宜之计的又一座纪念碑。租界亟需额外税收带来的资金，但它不需要中国纳税人的罢工，而后者似乎是若不延期就无法避免的后果。

表面上看，中国纳税人的态度完全是自私且错误的。但另一方面，许多同样的中国纳税人正遭受经济惩罚，与之相比，迄今为止资金充裕的工部局所面临的任何潜在困难在他们看来都微不足道。

对于那些怀疑上海成千上万中国人处于经济绝境的人而言，工部局住房委员会的调查结论非常值得重新审视——在这种绝境中，多支付一美元或二十美分都显得如高山般难以逾越。

上海经济方面小组委员会称，“可能没有哪个工人家庭拥有充足的住房。”人们忍受住房不足并非因为喜欢，而是因为他们处于维持生存水平线以下的境地。如果他们有足够多的钱支付更高的税款，他们会立刻把这些钱花在更好的住宿或食物上。调查发现，“工人家庭的典型月收入”约为25美元，其中每月仅能支付约5美元作为租金，即每人约1美元。更为重要的是附录三，其中宣称：“发现无论是非熟练工人、半熟练工人还是熟练工人，其生活开支均超出所得工资”，导致整个人口逐渐陷入债务之中。

这不是那种可以指望人们对生活成本哪怕最轻微的增加都泰然处之的人群画像。他们的反应是露出牙齿进行抗争；我们能责怪他们吗？如果他们的受教育程度包含一些市政问题的知识，这也不太可能激发他们缴纳更多税款的愿望，因为他们知道，那些分享额外税款收益的人，并不会比以往更紧密地体恤他们自身的艰难时世。不用说，像工部局乐队这样的福利设施远远超出他们的理解范围，我们可以将其排除在所有考量之外；但我们不能排除在考量之外的，是他们或许模糊却顽固坚持的信念：附近没有人比他们——上海的华人工人——处境更糟糕。

然而另一方面，没有人会主张上海广大产业工人的水平应决定租界的行政水平。任何甚至接近承认这一点的步骤都会……

唯一能做之事已在一定程度上付诸实施：使租界事务的管理尽可能具有商业效率且节约，特别是不失时机地为华人特殊利益服务，毕竟华人不仅在人数上超过外籍居民，而且支付了租界大部分税收收入。

在我们看来，在诸如支持今年夏天进行膳食厨房实验项目等问题上，工部局完全走上了正轨。该项目虽小，但意义重大；从中可以为目前遭受营养不良和饮食缺乏症困扰的贫困华人带来巨大的益处，据称，只要通过适当的实验（已为此做出安排）宣传正确的食物和制备方法，无需增加食物成本即可克服这些问题。在中文报刊上对此类项目进行宣传，将在很大程度上向中国纳税人表明，工部局已意识到华人的需求。

我们毫不迟疑地指出，租界的记录一贯显示出日益认识到有必要给予该地区华人居民应有的待遇，或许（在教育等方面）甚至比按缴纳税款比例计算的精确待遇还要多一些。但必须让公众知晓这一事实，并且如果在无需让步的情况下能够达成妥协，就应避免代价高昂的冲突。

正是基于这最后一点理由（如果没有其他理由的话），可以为目前的税率延期找到正当性。现在不是通过哪怕是看似专断的行动来引发争斗的时候。我们相信华人董事在承诺若能给予额外时间便支持税率上调一事上是完全真诚的，而向他们民众展示这种上调的必要性，在很大程度上必须是他们的任务。考虑到租界内许多华人的经济状况，这项任务并不容易，必须以坚定为主，辅以策略，特别是利用手头可用的宣传手段，就全部事实对华籍纳税人进行教育。

比以往任何时候都更有必要的是，这些事实应向公众公开，并经受最严格的审查。华人是精明的买家，不倾向于购买“盲盒里的猪”（指不明底细之物）。对他们来说，税率上调是一件需要推销技巧的事情——而商品则是良好的治理，并饰以新的、令人欢迎的社会责任意识的增长。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES; FRIDAY, - APRIL 9, 1937

Possible
Delay In
Rate Rise

Well-Informed Assertion
That Matter Is Under
Reconsideration

CHINESE OPPOSITION
IS EXPLAINED

Indication was given last night from a highly reliable Chinese source closely connected with Shanghai Municipal Council affairs. that the date for the coming into effect of the budgetary proposal to increase the General Municipal Rate from 14 to 16 per cent. may be postponed in deference to the wishes of the Chinese community.

The date set in the Budget, to be submitted for the approval of rate-payers at the Annual General Meeting to be held on Wednesday next, is July 1, but, according to the information given personally to a representative of "The Shanghai Times," there are further discussions in progress as a result of which developments might be expected.

Much opposition to the prospective increase has been expressed by Chinese Councillors and others, and it was in order to express that opposition that none of the Chinese members of the Council attended the meeting held on Wednesday afternoon. It was planned to issue a statement, through the Chinese Ratepayers' Association, yesterday afternoon, but, in consequence of an exchange of views with foreign members of the Council, no such statement was issued because of the prospect, it was said, that the Council would decide upon a postponement of the enforcement date.

The Chinese view, this journal was informed, was not opposition for all time to a rate increase, but opposition to an increase this year in view of the economic conditions prevailing. Further economy should first be attempted, and if it is then found that a rate increase is unavoidable, the Chinese councillors will give their support. But this should not be before next year—until there has been sufficient time to see how far further economies can help the Council to balance its budget.

延迟

消息灵通人士断言
此事正在
重新考虑中

解释
华人反对意见

昨晚，一位与上海公共租界工部局事务密切相关的可靠华人消息来源表示，出于对华人社区意愿的尊重，预算提案中将一般市政捐率从14%提高到16%的生效日期可能会推迟。

预算中设定的日期是7月1日，该预算将于下周三举行的年度大会上提交纳税人批准；但是，根据亲自向《字林西报》代表提供的信息，目前正在进一步讨论，预计会有后续发展。

华人董事及其他人士对拟议的增税表示了强烈反对，为了表达这种反对，没有任何一名华人董事出席周三下午举行的会议。原计划昨天下午通过华人纳税人协会发表声明，但由于与外籍董事交换了意见，据说鉴于工部局可能会决定推迟执行日期，因此未发表此类声明。

本报获悉，华人的观点并非永远反对税率上调，而是鉴于当前的经济状况，反对今年上调。应首先尝试进一步节约开支，如果随后发现税率上调不可避免，华人董事将给予支持。但这不应早于明年——直到有足够的时间观察进一步节约能在多大程度上帮助工部局平衡预算。

THE CHINA PRESS, THURSDAY, APRIL 8, 1937
CHINESE BOYCOTT LAST
MEET OF OLD COUNCIL

Councillors Absent As
Protest Over Attitude
On Municipal Rates

ARNHOLD SPEECH
UNDER REVIEW

Present Body Concludes
Year Filled With
Notable Activity

As a gesture of protest against
the tactics of the Shanghai Muni-
cipal Council in flouting and over-
riding their opposition to an in-
crease in municipal rates, the five
Chinese Councillors, as a body,
absented themselves from the Coun-
cil meeting yesterday.
A quorum, however, was obtained
to hold the meeting, which heard
the preliminary reading of Chair-
man H. E. Arnhold's speech to the
Foreign Ratepayers' Meeting on
April 14.
Yesterday's meeting was the last
before the 1936-37 Council goes out
of office next week. As the curtain
was drawn to a year's stirring
drama of municipal affairs, the last
act, made prominent by the absence
of the Chinese Councillors, depicted
much of the strife which charac-
terised the outgoing Council's
career.
Recorded in the history book of
Settlement politics during 1936 and
1937 is the efforts of the Council to
tighten its purse strings, which pro-
voked unbridled opposition during
the entire course of the Councillors
12 months' in office.
1st Tackle Fire Brigade
First act of the outgoing Council
in trimming its expenditure was
embodied in the Fire Brigade econo-
my measures, which, by reducing
watch towers, machines, fire
stations and personnel, resulted in
the saving of some $250,000 a year.
The economy axe next fell on a
number of temporary organisa-
tions set up during the past years
by the Council. By January 1 this
year, the ricksha Board and the
Press Information Office, both of
which had done useful and neces-
sary service for the Council, were
abolished out of economic necessity.
This measure again cut Council
expenditure down by a round $100,-
000 a year.
Greatest of all the savings was
worked out by the Staff Economy
Committee, whose measures in-
cidentally, provided the biggest
amount of argument and opposi-
tion. By revising pay schedules,
cutting down benefits and other
measures, the Council Committee
managed to decrease expenditure by
$1,000,000 a year. This measure
was approved by the Council and
will become operative July 1.

Seek Rate Increase
Climaxing its 12 months of axe-
wielding activity, the Council short-
ly before going out of office sought
to increase the revenue of the
S.M.C. by recommending a 2 per
cent increase in municipal rates.
This question is now being stren-
uously opposed by the Chinese rate-
payers, who threaten a "tax boy-
cott" as retaliation.
Apart from financial problems,
the Council, during the year, came
face to face with the usual quota
of thorny questions arising from
the long-standing issues of public
rickshas, outside roads and factory
inspection.
The credit of finally settling the
controversial factory inspection
issue barely escaped the 1936-37
Council when the draft agreement
it approved was thrown out by the
Consular Body.
On the public ricksha question, the
only accomplishment for which it
will take credit is the proposed re-
duction of 484 rickshas. The enforce-
ment of this measure was delayed
until June following a compromise
to avert a straight showdown with
the ricksha owners.
Road Issue Climax
The chief development during the
year on the extra-Settlement road
issue was the memorable tax siege
on a block of houses in the Yu
Yuen Road area. After arousing
much opposition and ill-feeling
among Chinese residents, the Coun-
cil decided to call off the war
following a tentative fiscal arrange-
ment with the City Government of
Greater Shanghai.
Other highlights of the year in-
cluded the problem arising out of
the miscount of the ballots, the
parking regulations, the boiler re-
gulations and the new ruling on
tuberculin-tested milk.
At the meeting yesterday five
Council members, one American
and four British, were sitting for
their last time. These members
scheduled to retire are Mr. H. E.
Arnhold, Chairman, Brig.-Gen. E.
B. Macnaghten, Mr. W. J. Kes-
wick, Mr. G. E. Mitchell, and Mr.
C. D. Calhoun.

《大美晚报》，1937年4月8日，星期四
华人抵制
旧董事会最后一次会议

董事缺席以抗议
在市政捐率问题上的
态度

回顾
阿诺尔德演讲

现任机构结束
充满显著活动的一年

作为一种抗议姿态，反对上海公共租界工部局无视并压制他们对市政捐率上调的反对意见的策略，五名华人董事集体缺席了昨天的董事会会议。
然而，会议达到了法定人数得以举行，会上初步宣读了主席H. E. Arnhold（阿诺尔德）定于4月14日在外籍纳税人大会上发表的讲话。
昨天的会议是1936-37届董事会下周卸任前的最后一次会议。随着这一年市政事务动荡戏剧的落幕，最后一幕因华人董事的缺席而引人注目，描绘了即将离任的董事会任期内特有的许多冲突。
在1936年和1937年的租界政治史册中，记载了工部局收紧财政的努力，这在董事们12个月的任期内引发了肆无忌惮的反对。
首先着手消防队
即将离任的董事会削减开支的第一项举措体现在消防队的节约措施中，通过减少瞭望塔、车辆、消防站和人员，每年节省约25万美元。
节约的大刀接下来砍向了过去几年由工部局设立的一些临时机构。到今年1月1日，人力车管理委员会和新闻情报处这两个曾为工部局提供有用且必要服务的机构，因经济需要而被撤销。这一措施再次使工部局的支出每年减少整整10万美元。
最大的节约成果是由职员节约委员会实现的，其措施顺便也引发了最大程度的争论和反对。通过修订薪资表、削减福利和其他措施，工部局委员会成功将支出每年减少100万美元。该措施已获工部局批准，将于7月1日生效。

寻求税率上调
在挥动斧头削减开支的12个月活动达到高潮之际，工部局在即将卸任前夕，建议将市政捐率提高2%，以增加上海公共租界工部局的收入。
这一问题目前正遭到华人纳税人的强烈反对，他们威胁以“抗税”作为报复。
除了财政问题外，工部局在这一年中还面临着一贯数量的棘手问题，这些问题源于长期存在的公共人力车、越界筑路和工厂检查等问题。
1936-37届工部局差点就能获得最终解决颇具争议的工厂检查问题的功劳，但其批准的协议草案被领事团驳回。
在公共人力车问题上，它唯一能引以为豪的成就就是提议减少484辆人力车。为避免与人力车主直接摊牌，达成妥协后，该措施的实施被推迟至六月。
道路问题高潮
这一年越界筑路问题的主要发展是愚园路地区一组房屋发生的著名的税务围困事件。在激起中国居民的强烈反对和不满情绪后，工部局在与大上海市政府达成临时财政安排后，决定停止这场“战争”。
当年的其他亮点包括因选票误计产生的问题、停车规定、锅炉规定以及关于经结核菌素测试牛奶的新规定。
在昨天的会议上，五名董事会成员，一名美国人和四名英国人，最后一次列席。这些预定退休的成员是：主席H. E. Arnhold（阿诺尔德）先生、E. B. Macnaghten（麦克纳格顿）准将、W. J. Keswick（凯瑟克）先生、G. E. Mitchell（米切尔）先生和C. D. Calhoun（卡尔霍恩）先生。

THE CHINA PRESS, TUESDAY, MARCH 30, 1937
Tax Strike Threatened 20918
In Chinese Opposition
To S. M. C. Rate Hike

Native Taxpayers Rally
Widespread Support
Against Increase

REPETITION OF
'27 EVENTS SEEN

Powerful Organizations
Express Solidarity
Against Paying

Events which might easily lead to the re-enactment of the 1927 Settlement-wide tax strike are today rapidly moving toward a climax as the Chinese community continues its agitation against the decision of the Shanghai Municipal Council to ask for a 2 per cent increase in rates.

The first Special District Citizens' Association, which last week raised the general anti-tax hike war-cry, announced yesterday that it had addressed a letter to the Council asking the latter to retract its decision.

This letter is generally expected to bring matters to an issue, as the Council, in replying to the communication, has either to accept or reject the request put forward by the citizens' body.

As the campaign gathered force during the week-end, speculation was rife as to what step the Chinese would take in the event that the Council adhered to its time-honored "standpat" policy and turned down all overtures for a re-opening of the question.

Strike Not Improbable

Heads of the leading Settlement organizations, including powerful guilds, residents' associations and merchant groups, when contacted by The China Press yesterday did not deny that a strike against tax payments is within the realm of possibility if the hike, approved by the Foreign Ratepayers' General Meeting, is put into effect.

These people recalled that in 1927 Chinese Settlement residents successfully "boycotted" the 2 per cent rate increase which the Council wanted to put into operation at that time. The strike lasted for nearly a whole month, and in order to break the deadlock, Mr. Yu Ya-ching was finally asked to mediate.

As a result of the tax war, which was called mainly to fight the "taxation without representation" status then in effect, the Chinese won the right of having three members of their nationality to sit on the Council.

Object To Methods

From the viewpoints of many Settlement Chinese residents, the present struggle against a rate increase is primarily based on their objection against "steamrollering" tactics used by the Council in getting the measure formally adopted. In other words, a portion of the Chinese ratepayers are incensed not by the rate hike per se, but by the allegedly high-handed methods used in driving the measure through.

It was pointed out that the strenuous objection raised against the hike by the Chinese Councillors, despite the fact that they represent a section of the community which pays more than 65 per cent of the Settlement taxes, was "muffled" and overridden. The resolution was driven through the Council with a bare majority of six against five votes.

For the Chinese ratepayers, the action of the Council has no available remedy. The financial measures, according to the present practice, will be brought up for approval or rejection at the Foreign Ratepayers' meeting. If it is endorsed by that body, the hike will become effective, and the decision of the foreign ratepayers will be final.

The Chinese Ratepayers' Meeting will not be asked to approve the measure, according to the present practice, and whatever action it might take will have no effect in preventing the measures from becoming operative.

No Redress

Thus, the Chinese ratepayers as a body, unendowed with the right to review the Council's financial measures, are compelled to take other effective steps to make its objection heard if its present anti-tax hike campaign is unheeded by the Council.

At the present time, although the general opinion of the Chinese ratepayers is unanimously against any form of rate increase, a compromise to settle the dispute is believed to be still acceptable. Such a compromise would have to include the conditional postponement of the rate hike for, say, six months. In other words, the 2 per cent raise should be put off until January 1937. If the municipal financial condition is unimproved by that time, the rate increase would then put into operation.

Unless such a compromise or some other solution similar to that is worked out and put into effect, observers believe that the present situation will ultimately lead to an expensive and unpleasant showdown.

The Chinese Ratepayers Association of the French Concession, at a meeting held yesterday, decided to respond to the campaign of Chinese ratepayers of the International Settlement to oppose the 2 per cent increase in municipal tax proposed by the Shanghai Municipal Council.

The Association in Frenchtown was to send an official representation on the question to the Shanghai Municipal Council, while letters of sympathy and support will be sent to the Chinese Ratepayers Association of the International Settlement and other Chinese groups opposed to proposed hike in municipal rate.

S. M. F.

《字林西报》，1937年3月30日，星期二
威胁发起抗税罢工 20918
华人反对
工部局加征捐税

本地纳税人集结
获得广泛支持
反对增税

被视为
“27年事件”重演

有力团体
表达团结
拒绝缴纳税款

随着华人社群持续抗议上海公共租界工部局要求增加2%捐税的决定，可能导致1927年全租界抗税罢工重演的事件正迅速走向高潮。

上周率先发出反对加税普遍号召的第一特区市民协会，昨日宣布已致函工部局，要求后者撤销其决定。

这封信预计将使事态明朗化，因为工部局在回复该信函时，要么接受、要么拒绝这一市民团体提出的请求。

随着周末期间运动势头增强，人们纷纷猜测，如果工部局坚持其历来不变的“维持现状”政策，并拒绝所有重新审议该问题的提议，华人将采取何种行动。

罢工并非不可能

包括有力量的同业公会、居民协会和商帮在内的租界主要团体负责人，昨日在接受《字林西报》采访时并未否认，如果经外侨纳税人大会批准的加税措施付诸实施，发起抗税罢工是有可能的。

这些人回顾道，1927年，租界华人居民成功“抵制”了工部局当时试图实施的2%捐税增加。罢工持续了近一个月，为了打破僵局，最终请虞洽卿先生出面调解。

这场主要为对抗当时实行的“无代表权而征税”状况而发起的抗税斗争，使华人赢得了在工部局拥有三名本族籍董事的权利。

反对手段

从许多租界华人居民的观点来看，目前反对加税的斗争，主要是基于他们反对工部局在正式通过该措施时使用的“强行推进”战术。换言之，部分华人纳税人感到愤怒的并非加税本身，而是据称在推动该措施通过时所使用的高压手段。

有人指出，尽管华人董事所代表的社群缴纳了租界65%以上的税款，但他们针对加税提出的强烈反对意见却被“压制”并否决。该决议在工部局以六票对五票的微弱多数强行通过。

对于华人纳税人而言，工部局的这一行动没有可用的补救办法。根据现行惯例，财政措施将提交外侨纳税人大会批准或否决。如果得到该机构认可，加税将生效，且外侨纳税人的决定将是最终决定。

根据现行惯例，华人纳税人大会不会被要求批准该措施，其可能采取的任何行动都无法阻止该措施生效。

无处申诉

因此，作为一个整体，华人纳税人无权审查工部局的财政措施，如果目前的反加税运动被工部局忽视，他们将被迫采取其他有效步骤，使其反对意见被听到。

THE CHINA PRESS, THURSDAY, MARCH 25, 1937

AN INCREASE IN RATE

As long foreshadowed, the prospect for the residents to pay an additional 2 per cent by way of municipal rate is becoming surer than ever. The Shanghai Municipal Council has been working for months to try to balance its budget, and so far no apparent success has crowned its efforts. As the easiest way out the proposal to increase the municipal rate naturally commands a ready hearing.

While we may sympathise with the Council for its desire of a balanced budget, we cannot overlook the hard lot of the ratepayers. On the one hand, the average wage-earner in Shanghai has had to endure repeated pay cuts with no hope of their restoration to former level in the near future, while on the other the Council has continually granted increases in the charges levied by the public utilities. If the municipal rate should be increased at the present moment, the masses will be hit the hardest, and what the Council may gain will not be sufficient to counter-balance what the community may lose as the result of dissatisfaction and unrest.

If the Council had exhausted all means of economy, an increase in the municipal rate may perhaps be justified. Yet the Chinese members of the Council have repeatedly suggested certain measures which the Council has seen fit to ignore. For instance, we may cite the following:
1. The exchange allowance to foreign members of the Municipal staff which this year cost the S.M.C. around $1,600,000;
2. The money spent in maintaining the Municipal Orchestra;
3. The annual expenses of supporting the Russian Regiment of the S.V.C.;
4. The staggering increase in the expenditure of the Police Force which this year cost the Council some $8,000,000.

Until the Council has carried out these sensible measures of retrenchment or until it can offer valid explanation for its inability so to carry out, any proposal to impose further tax burden on the residents, irrespective of conditions elsewhere, will surely meet with general opposition.

在过去几周里，继《字林西报》披露拟议增税的报道之后，据悉华董对工部局的财务状况进行了详尽审查。他们根据调查结果准备了反对拟议增税的理由书。预计他们将在今天下午的工部局会议上提交这份理由书。

据悉，昨晚华董在一次特别会议上再次审议了整个理由书，期间审查了一份在专家协助下编制的市政财政概况。

虽然华董准备的理由书中包含的具体要点并未明确披露，但《字林西报》获悉，以下项目可能会被提出：

1. 支付给工部局外籍职员的汇兑津贴，今年使工部局耗费约1,600,000元；

2. 用于维持工部局管弦乐队的费用；

3. 支援上海义勇队（S.V.C.）俄国分队的年度开支；

4. 警务处开支惊人增长，今年使工部局耗费约□□□,□□□元。
